_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Tata Chemicals (consolidated, Rs crore). Built by operating unit, the way the company reports to analysts: India (standalone), US (TCNA), UK (TCE), Kenya (Magadi), Singapore (Novabay) and Rallis India (100%); a seventh line removes inter-company sales. Each unit grows revenue and earns an EBITDA margin; group EBITDA = sum of units (company basis, before JV share). History is attributable to Tata Chemicals' shareholders (Screener Net Profit replaced by Profit for EPS, see tools/authoring/TATACHEM.patch.js). Valued on sum of the parts, as the street does: each geography on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA, the Rallis stake and quoted Tata-group shares at market value less a 20% holding-company discount, less net debt, pension provisions and minorities.

segments.name: India (standalone)
segments._why: FY26 revenue +9% on the Mithapur soda ash (+230 kt) and bicarb (+140 kt) expansions; Q1FY27 +10% (salt volumes +20%, soda ash spot price +Rs2,000/t). FY27 +7%: Q1 actual, then ~+6% as bicarb contracts lost in Q1 are partly won back. FY28 +6%: 82.5 KTPA IVSD salt from Q1FY28 and dense ash from Q3FY28, but the dense ash line replaces the cement plant. FY29 +8%: precipitated silica (Q4FY28, under review) and the 210 KTPA Valinokkam salt plant (Q2FY29).
segments._marginWhy: FY26 19.7%; Q1FY27 28.4% included low-cost coal inventory. Management calls ~18% sustainable; coal, limestone and freight costs rise if the Middle East conflict runs past October. FY27 21% (Q1 actual, ~19% for Q2-Q4); FY28 19.5%; FY29 20% as salt and silica add higher-margin volume.

segments.name: US (Tata Chemicals North America)
segments._why: FY26 revenue -6% (exports to South-East Asia cut, lower prices). Q1FY27 +16% on volumes (614 kt) and a weaker rupee. FY27 +9%; FY28 +6% as the Searles Valley customer contracts bought on 11-Sep-2026 (more than 0.5 mt over two years) add volume; FY29 +2%.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin fell from 24% (FY23) to 6% (FY26) and 0.2% in Q1FY27 (US$1/t) as Chinese export prices (US$160-180/t FOB) made SE Asia exports unremunerative 'at least through the year'. FY27 2.5% (~Rs45 cr a quarter after Q1); FY28 7% and FY29 9% (roughly US$15-20/t) on domestic contract volumes and slow Chinese rationalisation, still far below the US$40/t of FY25-Q1FY26.

segments.name: UK (Tata Chemicals Europe)
segments._why: Since the Lostock soda ash plant closed (Jan-2025) the UK sells salt, pharma salt and bicarb made from imported TCNA ash; FY26 revenue -27% on the closure. Q1FY27 +6%. FY27 +8% (sterling, new pharma salt volumes); 4% a year after.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 6.0%; Q1FY27 -1% after ~GBP2.4 mn of one-offs (EU ETS sale loss, prior-period items). Management expects the UK to be EBITDA positive in FY27. 5% / 7% / 8%.

segments.name: Kenya (Magadi)
segments._why: Natural soda ash exported mainly to Asia; FY26 revenue -4%; Q1FY27 +7% on volumes. 3% a year.
segments._marginWhy: FY23 50%, FY26 17%, Q1FY27 1% as HFO fuel costs jumped with oil (hedged only to October) and export prices fell. FY27 10%; FY28-29 15-16% if fuel normalises, below the FY24-26 average of ~25%.

segments.name: Singapore (Novabay)
segments._why: Premium pharma-grade bicarb plant (60 KTPA) acquired 19-Mar-2026, consolidated from 1-Jan-2026, so FY26 holds one quarter (Rs61 cr). Q1FY27 revenue Rs60 cr: FY27 ~Rs245 cr (+300% on one quarter), then +5% a year; the 40 KTPA expansion has no date yet.
segments._marginWhy: Q1FY27 EBITDA Rs5 cr (8%); integration under way. 8-10%.

segments.name: Rallis India (100%)
segments._why: Crop protection and seeds; FY26 revenue +9%, Q1FY27 +7% (volumes and prices). 8-9% a year, in line with its FY22-26 range.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 12.6%; Q1FY27 18% (seasonal peak); FY23-26 range 7-13%. 13.5-14%. Tata Chemicals owns 55.04%; the 44.96% minority is deducted in the tax line.

segments.name: Inter-company and other adjustments
segments._why: Consolidated revenue less the sum of units: -Rs188 cr in FY26 (UK buys TCNA soda ash, SPV and other adjustments); Q1FY27 -Rs50 cr. Grows with the units.
segments._marginWhy: Zero: the EBITDA difference between consolidated and units was Rs+4 cr in FY26 and Rs+2 cr in Q1FY27.

_unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any unit (India standalone carries head office)
_unallocWhy: Head-office costs sit inside the India standalone numbers; consolidated EBITDA equalled the sum of units within Rs4 cr in FY26.
_capexWhy: FY26 Rs1,205 cr. FY27: ~Rs1,300 cr guided in May, then 'around depreciation' (~Rs1,200 cr) in July: Rs1,250 cr. FY28-29: maintenance (~Rs800-900 cr) plus the Rs1,525 cr project list (IVSD Rs100 cr, dense ash Rs135 cr, silica Rs775 cr, Valinokkam Rs515 cr) phased over FY27-29; management intends to stay at or below depreciation.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs1,201 cr = 4.2% of average gross block (Rs28,610 cr); Q1FY27 Rs336 cr (Rs1,344 cr annualised) after capitalisation. 4.4% lands FY27 at ~Rs1,350 cr. Includes ~Rs100 cr a year amortisation of US mining rights.
_treasuryWhy: Net debt company; other income entered separately.
_otherIncomeWhy: Gross other income + share of JV profit: FY26 Rs483 cr (Rs316 cr other income incl. dividends from Titan and other Tata stakes, Rs167 cr JV share from IMACID and Tata Industries); Q1FY27 Rs39 cr (IMACID shut on sulphur costs, JV share -Rs17 cr). FY27E gross ~Rs350 cr (other income ~Rs250 cr, JV ~Rs100 cr as IMACID restarts), FY28E Rs420 cr, FY29E Rs440 cr (back near FY25-26 levels). Engine workaround for FY27E only: the group makes a loss after tax and minorities while pre-tax profit is close to zero, which a tax rate cannot express, so FY27E 'other income' is shown NET of tax on profitable units (~Rs122 cr: India, Rallis, Kenya, less a US credit) and minorities (~Rs217 cr), i.e. 350 - 122 - 217 = 11, with a zero tax rate.
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs590 cr; Q1FY27 Rs148 cr. Management expects FY27 debt near Mar-26 levels (net debt ex-leases Rs5,961 cr; Rs5,692 cr in Jun-26).
_taxWhy: The tax line also carries minorities (engine workaround, as in UPL and Coromandel): Rallis 44.96% (~Rs117-148 cr a year) and the ALCAD US partnership 50% (~Rs99 cr in FY26). Tax itself is paid by India, Rallis and Kenya while UK losses earn no credit and the US books only a partial credit after the Rs182 cr DTA write-off. FY27E: 0% because tax and minorities are netted in other income (see _otherIncomeWhy). FY28E: tax ~Rs190 cr + minorities ~Rs235 cr on PBT ~Rs605 cr = 70%. FY29E: ~Rs240 cr + ~Rs248 cr on ~Rs900 cr = 54%. The DCF applies the FY29E rate to all later years, i.e. it values only Tata Chemicals' share of cash flows and assumes US losses stay untaxed: conservative.
_payoutWhy: DPS Rs11 for FY25 and FY26 (119% of FY25 EPS; paid despite the FY26 loss). FY27E: 0% in the model because EPS is negative; the Rs11 FY26 dividend paid in FY27 (Rs280 cr) is deducted separately in the SOTP. FY28E 100% of EPS (~Rs7) and FY29E 70% (~Rs11): we assume the board cuts the dividend while the group earns little.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). Tata Chemicals carries debt, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1) weighted ~72%, post-tax cost of debt ~5.6% weighted ~28% (net debt incl. leases ~Rs6,800 cr vs ~Rs15,600 cr market value) = ~11.0%, which beta 0.75 produces.
dcf._tgWhy: Soda ash, salt and bicarb demand grows with nominal GDP in India and slower abroad; 5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Group revenue growth fades to 6% (India 8-9%, overseas 2-3%).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades to 6% of revenue (maintenance ~Rs800-900 cr); depreciation 6.5% of revenue (FY26 8.2%, falling as revenue grows on a mature asset base). Long-run EBITDA margin 16%: the FY22-26 average was 17.6% (peak 22.8% in FY23, trough 12.4% in FY26).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: China rationalises capacity and export prices recover towards US$220-250/t; the US earns US$30-40/t again with the Searles Valley volumes; India holds 21-22% margins; Kenya fuel costs normalise; Tata Sons lists, giving value to the 2.53% stake (we add Rs5,000 cr, half the low end of press estimates).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Chinese oversupply persists through FY29: US EBITDA stays near US$10/t, Kenya margins stay low, India slips to 17-18% as new bicarb capacity and imports compete and coal/limestone costs stay high, and Rallis margins revert to ~12%; no Tata Sons listing.

parts.name: India (standalone)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Street 7x (Motilal Oswal, FY28E) to 9x (JM Financial, Sep-27E). GHCL, the closest Indian soda ash peer, trades at ~5x trailing; DCM Shriram ~9.4x. 8x: a premium to GHCL for salt, bicarb and prebiotics (~45% of India revenue, stickier food/pharma demand), no more because returns are below the cost of capital.

parts.name: US (TCNA)
parts.note: Street 5x (Motilal Oswal) to 6.5x (JM). Low-cost natural soda ash, but price-taker against Chinese exports; Sep-28E EBITDA already assumes a partial recovery from ~zero. 6x.

parts.name: UK (TCE)
parts.note: Street 5x (Motilal Oswal, Europe+Africa) to 8x (JM). Salt and bicarb only since Lostock closed; thin margins and a pension deficit: 5x.

parts.name: Kenya (Magadi)
parts.note: Street 5x (Motilal Oswal) to 6.5x (JM). Exporter of natural ash into the most competitive Asian markets; fuel-cost exposed: 5x.

parts.name: Singapore (Novabay)
parts.note: Pharma-grade bicarb, customer-approved and stickier than soda ash; small (~Rs25 cr EBITDA). Valued like India: 8x.

parts.name: Rallis India: 55.04% stake at market value less 20%
parts.metricLabel: 55.04% × Rs3,883 cr market value (Rs199.73 on 30-Sep-2026) × (1 − discount)
parts.note: Street method (Motilal Oswal, JM: 20% holding-company discount). Bull 10%, bear 30% discount. Rallis EBITDA is therefore not valued again, and its 44.96% minority is not deducted again.

parts.name: Quoted Tata-group shares at market value less 20%
parts.metricLabel: Rs8,297 cr at 30-Sep-2026 closes (Titan Rs6,342 cr, Indian Hotels Rs865 cr, Tata Steel Rs570 cr, others Rs520 cr) × (1 − discount)
parts.note: Mar-26 holdings (AR FY26) at NSE closes on 30-Sep-2026; Tata Investment at Mar-26 book. Street: 20% discount (Motilal Oswal, JM); bull 10%, bear 30%. Some shares were sold in Q1FY27 (undisclosed): a small overstatement.

parts.name: Less: quoted shares at Mar-26 book (inside model net cash)
parts.metricLabel: Removes the book value already counted in the model's cash and investments
parts.note: The model's net cash includes all investments at Mar-26 book; the quoted shares are valued separately above. JVs (IMACID, Tata Industries, Rs1,460 cr), unquoted stakes (incl. Tata Sons at Rs57 cr) and liquid funds stay at book.

parts.name: Tata Sons stake (2.53%)
parts.metricLabel: Only in the bull case: Rs10,000 cr (low end of press estimates) less 50%
parts.note: No listing date: RBI rejected Tata Sons' de-registration on 11-Sep-2026, but Tata Trusts proposed a restructuring that could avoid listing (29-Sep-2026). No broker values it. Base and bear carry it at book (Rs57 cr, inside net cash).

parts.name: Less: Rallis net cash (belongs to Rallis' market value)
parts.metricLabel: Rallis Mar-26 cash Rs45 cr + investments Rs505 cr − borrowings Rs61 cr
parts.note: Rallis is valued at market, which already includes its cash; removing it from consolidated net cash avoids counting it twice.

parts.name: Less: ALCAD partner's 50% (US minority)
parts.metricLabel: Partner's share of profit (Rs99 cr in FY26) × the US multiple
parts.note: US EBITDA includes 100% of the ALCAD partnership; half of its profit belongs to the partner (AR FY26 note 18).

parts.name: Less: employee-benefit provisions (Mar-26)
parts.metricLabel: Consolidated pension and other employee-benefit provisions (AR FY26 note 21)
parts.note: Mostly UK and US pension deficits; the street deducts the same (Motilal Oswal Rs1,198 cr, JM Rs1,203 cr).

parts.name: Less: FY26 dividend paid in FY27
parts.note: Paid in Q2FY27; the model books no FY27 dividend because FY27E EPS is negative.

parts.name: Net cash at Sep-27E (model: cash and investments less borrowings incl. leases)
parts.note: Mar-26: cash Rs442 cr + investments Rs9,886 cr − borrowings incl. leases Rs8,001 cr = +Rs2,327 cr; after removing quoted shares at book this is net debt of ~Rs4,900 cr incl. leases and JVs at book.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Tata Chemicals (Motilal Oswal, JM Financial, Kotak): four geographies with very different economics, a listed subsidiary and a portfolio of Tata-group shares worth about half the market value.

methods.name: Group EV/EBITDA
methods.why: 7.3x = our own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (8.6x, trough year FY26 left out) less the 15% median de-rating of Indian commodity chemical peers; bull = the 8.6x median, bear = the 6.1x the stock traded at on 30-Sep-2026 (FY28E). One multiple on consolidated EBITDA (incl. 100% of Rallis), plus model net cash with all investments at book. Rougher than the SOTP: no holding-company discount on investments, no deduction for minorities or pensions.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at ~11% WACC, terminal growth 5%, plus model net cash (investments at book).
